SPOTIFY, RENTED VS OWNED (2026-09-17): monthly listeners fell 78% from the 2026-03-19 peak (26,217 to 5,859), but every owned-audience metric rose over the same period. Followers 504 to 1,238 with no down month ever; streams per listener 4.2 to 11.0; super listeners 3.7% to 11.0% of audience; save rate by era 3.61% to 5.36%. What collapsed was algorithmic subsidy, not the fanbase. Do not read monthly listeners as project health.

SPOTIFY, RELEASE LIFT IS DEAD: Banned Badge (Jan 2026) drove +1014% in 28-day streams. Every release since decayed: +45, +31, -22, -11, +13, +2, -25, -20, +15%. The last five are noise. Releasing is no longer a Spotify growth lever; releases now function as raw material for the video engine, not as stream drivers.

SPOTIFY, PER-SONG DECAY: average streams per song by era. Banned Badge 26,245 (13 songs), Heart Scales 10,470 (15), Pink Bois 5,239 (25), Pretty Rare Candies 3,409 (14). Down 87% while save rate rose 48%. More releases into a flat audience splits the same listeners; 25 Pink Bois songs earned fewer total streams than 13 Banned Badge songs.

SPOTIFY, THE FLOOR IS THE REAL METRIC: minimum daily streams (passive catalog demand with no push) ran ~2,300/day Feb-Jun 2026, then dropped to ~1,500/day Jul-Sep. That 35% floor decline is the genuine structural loss. Track the floor and follower count; ignore monthly listeners.

SPOTIFY, DISTRIBUTION IS 91% ALGORITHMIC: 129,449 playlist streams from Spotify-owned surfaces vs 12,709 from everything else. Of that 12,709, Erik's own Kirbai Pokedex is 5,857 and unprompted fan-built Kirbai playlists are 3,614 across 9 separate playlists with only 3-8 listeners each. No cushion under the algorithm.

CONVERSION GAP IS THE TOP OPPORTUNITY: the Runway Regi Reel reached 214,000 on Instagram; total Spotify followers are 1,238. A single video touched ~170x the entire follower base with near-zero conversion. This is a plumbing problem (CTA, link friction), not a reach or quality problem, and it is the highest-leverage fixable item in the dataset.

instagram.finding: The July 17 Instagram export fully supersedes the overlapping July 6 export. Baseline totals use one row per post ID.

facebook.finding: The export mixes videos and photo posts. Totals include both; the coverage block separates video count.

distroKid.finding: Only the newest cumulative DistroKid export is summarized. The selected ledger contains a small number of exact duplicate-looking rows, but there is no transaction ID proving they are accidental duplicates. Official totals therefore retain them and expose a deduplicated sensitivity check.

usageRules: Treat this file as a dated baseline, not live analytics.
Use Pulse and Revenue Engine when they contain a newer import.
Do not add overlapping Instagram exports together; deduplicate by Post ID.
Keep Kirbai separate from Kirby Henry, AELOW, and KURAO when discussing artist performance.
Label royalty figures with reporting coverage and warn that the newest sale month may be incomplete.
DistroKid Quantity means reported units and can include social-media uses, downloads, or other source types; do not relabel the total as streams.
Never infer causation from a high-performing post or track without a controlled comparison.

caveats: Monthly listeners is a trailing 28-day unique count. Algorithmic batches entering and aging out of that window cause cliff-shaped moves that do NOT reflect audience loss. Verify against daily streams before concluding decline.
The 2026-03-19 peak of 26,217 monthly listeners was an algorithmic batch, not a release. Daily streams held flat at ~3,000/day straight through the subsequent crash.
Song and playlist exports cover a trailing year only, so pre-Sept-2025 catalog is undercounted there.
